rulings.reason: The flag is correct on the bytes. EXTRACTED from SP\Dan\Dan_web_clean.txt: verse 1:8 has 'requested of the prince of the eunuchs' and verse 1:9 ends 'in the sight of the prince of the eunuchs', so the six flagged words are six consecutive WEB words of two verses inside the row's span Dan.1.8-Dan.1.16; 1:10 opens 'The prince of the eunuchs said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king' (verses 1:8 to 1:16 read in full). EXTRACTED from SP\Dan\tools\check_web_quotes.py lines 75-112 and 289-330: A6_MIN_WORDS is 5, the comparison set is the field's refs plus the row's own span, a run is skipped only when its first word begins inside a curly double quote, and the single exemption (lines 320-324) is a top-level parent_collection label; a prose field has none. MEASURED (work\t1.py, base copy): the suite on an unchanged copy reproduces 138 flags and this one web_quotes flag. Why not A: ruling A6 makes content the test whatever the delimiter; an exemption for a title used as a name would be a new class carved out of A6 by a same-family fallback execution (OW-25), it would leave web_quotes at FLAGS for both primaries and the close, and the officer's title alone ('the prince of the eunuchs') is five WEB words, so the class would recur. A script-checkable rewording costs one record. Why not B: MEASURED (work\t1.py, copy B, 'the fear voiced by “the prince of the eunuchs” (web:Dan.1.10)') it also returns to 137 flags, but it adds a web: reference to the field, moves one refs_mirror worklist entry from observed_substrate_signals to boundary_rationale, and puts a citation and the verb 'voiced' into a sentence that was a plain summary; and by the tool's rule (a run is protected only if its first word begins inside the quote) a bare 'of “the prince of the eunuchs”' would be expected still to flag, which I INFER from the code and did not run. C changes less. Why C adds no reading: 'the eunuchs' prince' is the same title with the same two nouns in a possessive, which is also the shape of the construct pair sar ha-sarisim at SP\Dan\Dan_oshb.txt Dan.1.10 (words 2-3); it selects no textual reading and touches no divided reading. The tier stays (INFERRED) as E4 set it for the whole sentence; no tier is raised. TESTED BEFORE ORDERING (work\t1.py, summarised by work\t2.py): on copy C the suite gives hard_status GREEN, dead_members [], triage_flags 137, web_quotes flag_count 0 and status GREEN, ngram7 GREEN; against the base copy, with the 'file' key left out, zero entries added and exactly the one web_quotes entry removed. MEASURED (work\t1.py, work\t3.py): the 'before' occurs once in the field and once in the whole file; the 'after' occurs zero times before; exactly one value differs (W1-002.boundary_rationale); 75 rows; zero CR bytes; G matches 2 before and 2 after; the four corpus-wide regexes read from E1 match the 'after' zero times and their counts in the field are unchanged ({"CWO-DAN-01": [0, 0, 0], "CWO-DAN-02": [0, 0, 0], "CWO-DAN-03": [0, 0, 0], "CWO-DAN-04": [0, 0, 0]}, as [old field, new field, the 'after' alone]). A weakness I leave standing: 'the fear of X' can be read as fear felt toward X; E4's wording had the same shape.
